pageProps.title: Salvation of a Saint
pageProps.review: The second full-length novel in Keigo Higashino's Detective Galileo series, this review of a mystery masterpiece deals with the ingenious tricks and the truth of a perfect crime created by the effort not to kill through the concepts of imaginary solutions and salvation.
pageProps.description: Salvation and a single day of judgment - Imaginary Solution
pageProps.content:
## Review As the second full-length novel of ```Detective Galileo```, it is a work that focuses more on the most classic proposition of mystery: how did they kill.
The two core keys that penetrate this work are the concepts of Imaginary Solution and Salvation. Imaginary Solution symbolizes a ```solution that is theoretically possible but can never exist in reality```, namely a perfect crime. On the other hand, Salvation holds the contradictory meanings of both a merciful act of sparing a life and a cold preparation process for certain judgment.
It seems to be a work that shakes the conventions of this genre in that it's about the ```effort not to kill``` rather than the effort to kill.
There are characters who approach a single goal, the truth, in different ways.
Personally, I think it's one of the most bold and ingenious tricks.
